cohort_rule: Named military posts, wartime training bases, and hospital/named unit opponents; explicit institutional continuity for identical labels and source notation variants; no aggregation by geography or service branch. 10 distinct families, 17 labels, 32 accepted games.

families.name: Naval Air Station North Island
families.identity_basis: U.S. Navy documents North Island commissioned as a naval air station in 1917, with its contemporary designation NAS San Diego before 1955. Source North Island NAS labels refer to this station team; do not combine with a generic San Diego Navy source label.

families.name: San Diego Amphibious Training Base
families.identity_basis: The Navy identifies the World War II amphibious training base created by 1943 authorization and commissioned January 1944 in Coronado. This military facility/team is separate from North Island NAS and Navy's San Diego repair base; location is institutional identity only, not H/A/N evidence.

accepted_rows.literal: at San Diego Amphibious Training Base

families.name: Santa Ana Army Air Base
families.identity_basis: Santa Ana Army Air Base established and activated February 1942, documented by Costa Mesa Historical Society and Army historical materials. Not Santa Ana Naval Air Station in Tustin or Santa Ana Junior College.

accepted_rows.literal: at Santa Ana Army Air Base

families.name: Camp Callan 57th Battalion
families.identity_basis: San Diego History Center identifies Camp Callan as a World War II Army training center constructed in 1940; original SDSU source identifies the 57th Battalion specifically. Keep battalion team separate from any general Camp Callan team. Historical game series independently appears as two contests in 1942-43.

families.name: San Diego Naval Hospital
families.identity_basis: U.S. Navy and San Diego History Center independently document Naval Hospital San Diego in Balboa Park from 1922 and during the war. Identity is its hospital team, not naval-air-station, San Diego Navy, or San Diego Marines team.

families.name: Section Base–Point Loma
families.identity_basis: The original source specifically names a Section Base–Point Loma team. 1941 Navy filing manual identifies San Diego Section Base and separate Point Loma repair base, while NPS documents Section Base boiler at Point Loma. Exact historical administrative relationship is not inferred: retain uniquely named source team as provisional, distinct from Fort Rosecrans and other Point Loma facilities.

families.name: Fort Rosecrans
families.identity_basis: Fort Rosecrans was a U.S. Army coastal-defense installation on Point Loma into the 1940s, documented by NPS and Navy. Do not merge with Naval Section Base Point Loma, Navy sub base, or another garrison.

families.name: San Bernardino Army Air Base
families.identity_basis: U.S. Air Force Civil Engineer Center histories establish name San Bernardino Army Airfield in 1942, later renamed Norton. Source's Army Air Base descriptive label retained; distinct from Santa Ana Army Air Base.

families.name: Luke Air Force Base
families.identity_basis: U.S. Air Force Luke heritage history establishes the reactivated installation as Luke Air Force Base on February 1, 1951, covering the source 1953-54 era. Source 'at' token is not H/A/N inference.

families.name: Presidio of San Francisco
families.identity_basis: National Park Service documents San Francisco Presidio functioning as U.S. Army installation and Sixth Army headquarters in 1950s. Specific post team remains distinct from San Francisco colleges or San Francisco-based military units.

separations_enforced: North Island NAS distinct from generic San Diego Navy label
San Diego Amphibious Training Base distinct from North Island NAS
Santa Ana Army Air Base distinct from Santa Ana Naval Air Station (Tustin)
Section Base–Point Loma distinct from Fort Rosecrans and unrelated Point Loma organizations
